Resolves #21138

Related: #20892, #20750, #21022, #21057, #21024, #21016, #21058, neomjs/neo-agent-brain#1764, neomjs/neo-agent-institution#989

Releases assigned outside contributors cleanly when they withdraw an issue claim, separates real releases from negations, active-work continuations, and scheduled deferrals, and documents how contributors return a claim:

- **Withdrawal & clause-anchored affirmative patterns (`buildScripts/util/claimResponse.mjs#isWithdrawal`):** Distinguishes real withdrawals (`"Unclaiming this..."`, `"I'm withdrawing my claim."`, `"Please unassign me."`, `"I'm stepping back..."`, `"Consider it available."`, `"Sorry, I can't work on this anymore."`, `"Giving up the claim."`, `"I'm no longer able to work on this."`) from non-affirmative prose via sentence/clause-anchored matching (`hasAffirmativeProseWithdrawal`: strips inline code/quoted strings, skips questions and conditional `if`/`unless`/`when` sentences, and anchors affirmative first-person subjects or imperatives to clause starts without backtracking quantifiers — rejecting `"I am not withdrawing my claim."`, `"I do not plan to withdraw my claim."`, `"I'm not considering withdrawing my claim."`, `"I do not think I should withdraw my claim."`, `"I have no plans at all to withdraw my claim."`, `"Please don't unassign me."`, questions, and quoted examples), active-work continuations (`CONTINUATION_PATTERN` evaluated before prose withdrawals, while explicit `/unclaim`/`/unassign` remains immediate), scheduled deferrals (`"I can't finish this before Friday, the PR comes Monday."`), and comments that also claim the issue (`CLAIM_PATTERNS`).
- **Release state, supersession & 3-day non-reset (`staleAssignees`, `holders`, `decideClaim`, `decideWithdrawal`):** Added `withdrawalMarker`, `renderWithdrawalReply`, and `decideWithdrawal` (judging the comment against the thread's latest state so a subsequent claim, assignment/unassignment transition, bot reply, or explicit withdrawal denial / continuation note supersedes an older withdrawal); outside assignees whose latest comment withdrew without a subsequent assignment hold nothing (`holders` skips them, keeping any open same-repo PR holder) and never reset the 3-day `CLAIM_WINDOW_DAYS` timer even when a prior unassignment call failed; after withdrawing/unassignment, `decideClaim` allows `/claim` re-entry without overwriting historical acceptance replies.
- **Workflow & contributor guide (`.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`):** Handles outside withdrawals alongside claims (checking collaborator permission before calling `removeAssignees`, verifying the updated `assignees` response before posting one deduplicated confirmation reply), and adds `/unclaim` / withdrawal guidance to `CONTRIBUTING.md` step 3.

Prescription checked: `buildScripts/util/claimResponse.mjs`, `.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` — owns the concern.

Evidence: L2 (Playwright unit tests exercising `decideWithdrawal`, `isWithdrawal`, `holders`, `staleAssignees`, `decideClaim`, linear-time clause matching, and the live `github-script` step in `.github/workflows/claim-responder.yml` across AC-1 through AC-6 on committed head `9b0489b8d2`) -> L3 required (AC-7 post-merge observation of the first real withdrawal by an assigned outside claimant). Residual: AC-7, Residual-Owner: #20892.

Thank you `@neo-opus-ada` and `@neo-gpt-emmy` for the CodeQL `js/redos` measurement and the 6 trailing-conditional / comma-split denial falsifiers (`"I will withdraw my claim if someone else would like it."`, `"/unclaim if someone else can finish it"`, `"I have not, and never will, withdraw my claim."`, `"Do not write: I withdraw my claim."`, `"It would be wrong to say, I withdraw my claim."`, `"I know I should not say, I cannot work on this anymore."`).

- **Commit `1b3d6c6525`:**
  - Restricted `SLASH_WITHDRAWAL_PATTERN` to standalone `/unassign` / `/unclaim` lines (`(?:[ \t]+me)?[ \t.!]*$`) with zero regex alternation, rejecting conditional slash lines like `"/unclaim if someone else can finish it"`.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge OR documented search (per guide §7.1):**

- **Challenge**: `cancel-in-progress: false` gives one running and one pending run per group. GitHub cancels an older *pending* run when a newer one queues, so a `/unclaim` that arrives while an earlier run is still busy can be dropped by a later comment's run. Each run re-reads the thread, and RA-2's latest-state rule keeps the outcome correct whichever runs survive. I'm recording this as the reason RA-2 matters beyond manual re-runs; it asks nothing extra.
